metaDescription: Four generators for a fifth wheel camper compared on running watts, 30 amp outlets, weight for a truck bed and real fuel behavior, with honest limits.
expertTake: The Westinghouse 5000 is the top pick for most fifth wheels because remote start, clean power and a data display come with a proven brand. The Genkins 4500 is the value pick for a lighter carry. Owners of big toy haulers with two or three air conditioners should consider a larger open-frame unit, which is outside this list.
introParagraphs: A fifth wheel is the heaviest towable most people own, and its electrical demand grows with its size. Larger models carry several roof air conditioners, a residential fridge and a bank of slide motors, so the generator choice is more about headroom than about carrying capacity.

Most owners tow with a pickup, which gives them a bed to carry the generator in, but also a limit on payload. The practical decision is how many watts you really need, how much weight the truck can spare and whether quiet matters at the sites you use.

products.name: Westinghouse 5000 Peak Watt Super Quiet Inverter, Remote Start
products.description:
Westinghouse built this machine around a feature that matters to a fifth wheel owner: remote start. With a key fob, you can fire the generator from inside the trailer on a cold morning, then shut it off from the couch after the air conditioner has cooled the cabin. The LED data center rotates through fuel level, output, remaining run time and voltage, so you can see in real time what the coach is drawing.

At 3,900 rated watts and a TT-30R outlet, it matches the typical one air conditioner rig. Power quality is under 3 percent total harmonic distortion, which is clean enough for a laptop, a TV and a CPAP. The telescoping handle and wheel kit make it easier to move around a campsite than an open-frame machine.

As a gasoline inverter of this size it is a mid-weight machine, and the remote start battery needs charging. Change the oil after the first 20 hours, since small inverter crankcases get hot. For long storage, use the monthly exercise and keep the fuel stabilized. Compared with the 4650 open frame it costs more but is noticeably quieter, and the extra 300 rated watts is the difference between a microwave running alongside the air conditioner or not. A fifth wheel owner who parks at state parks with generator quiet hours will feel that difference every evening, and at a state park with a generator curfew the quieter exhaust note is what keeps a neighbor from knocking.
products.bestFor: Single air conditioner fifth wheels that want remote start and clean power.
pros: Key fob remote start from inside the coach
Rotating display shows runtime and voltage
3,900 rated watts beats most 30 amp inverters
cons: A second air conditioner needs a bigger machine

products.name: Westinghouse 4650 Peak Watt Generator, 30A Outlet, 4 Gallon Tank
products.description:
An open-frame generator makes sense in a truck bed. It is cheaper per watt than an inverter, rolls on its own wheel kit and carries a four gallon tank with a fuel gauge that claims up to 14 hours of run time. The 3,600 running watts is also exactly the ceiling of a 30 amp circuit, so it covers the full circuit.

The cost is noise and refinement. It runs at a fixed engine speed, so it burns fuel at light load and is much louder than the 5000 inverter. It starts on a recoil pull, which is harder than the push-button or remote starts on the other units here. It offers both TT-30R and L5-30R outlets.

It arrives with oil, a funnel and a tool kit, so first starts are easy. For truck bed use, secure it with straps and a wheel chock, and keep it upright so oil does not flood the cylinder during transport. Stabilize the fuel before storage, and run the carburetor dry on a long winter break. A truck bed is a rough ride, so inspect the fuel cap seal and the recoil handle after long hauls, and never transport it with a full tank on a hot day since gasoline expands and can weep from the vent.
products.bestFor: Truck bed carry where cost and tank size matter more than noise.
pros: Four gallon tank claims up to 14 hours
3,600 running watts fills a 30 amp circuit
Lower cost per watt than inverter units
cons: Noticeably louder than the inverter models

products.name: Genkins 4500W Inverter Generator, 174cc, 63 lb
products.description:
Genkins aims at the owner who does not want to wrestle a heavy frame. At 63 pounds it is easy to lift into a truck bed, while 3,800 rated watts from a 174cc engine beats the Westinghouse 5000 on sustained output by a small margin. The 1.9 gallon tank claims up to 8 hours.

It is a pure sine wave inverter, so electronics are protected, and it runs quiet for its class. The trade is service and parts: Genkins is a newer brand with a thinner dealer network than Westinghouse. The 8 hour runtime is also shorter than the 14 hours of the open-frame 4650.

It is a good value for a fifth wheel owner who runs one air conditioner and needs a quiet machine. Keep the vents clear, run it monthly and use fresh fuel. Check the warranty terms and keep a spare spark plug and air filter, since parts availability is the first thing to test on a newer brand. Next to the Westinghouse 5000 it adds about 300 rated watts and loses remote start, so decide which of those you value more, and remember that a 63 pound machine is the one you will actually carry to a quiet corner of the site rather than leave on the truck tailgate.
products.bestFor: Owners who want a light, quiet inverter with high sustained output.
pros: 3,800 rated watts is the highest inverter figure here
Pure sine wave output for electronics
Quiet for a machine in this class
cons: Eight hour claim is shorter than the open frame
Brand has a thinner service network

products.name: AIVOLT 7500 Watt Dual Fuel Portable Generator, 322cc, Wheels
products.description:
This is the machine for a fifth wheel with two air conditioners. It is a 322cc dual fuel generator with a cast iron sleeve, rated at 7,500 peak watts, and it offers a 120/240 volt 14-30R outlet for RVs or a home transfer switch plus a 120 volt 30 amp outlet. The CO Watch-Guard system adds visual alerts and an automatic shutdown.

It is an open-frame wheeled unit, so it is heavier and louder than the inverter models, and the listing gives only a peak figure, so the running watts are lower. That makes it harder to size, and you should assume a sustained output well below 7,500. Propane lowers the number further.

Expect a bed-mounted carrier or a heavy ramp. Fuel flexibility is the draw: propane for storage, gasoline for full power. Run the machine monthly, charge the starter if electric, and keep the CO alert free of dust, because a clogged sensor can give false alerts that end a run for no reason. It is a good fit for a toy hauler that carries toys and needs more power. Peak capacity is roughly double that of the Westinghouse 4650, which is what a second roof unit needs, but you pay for it in weight and noise, so plan a ramp and a location for it away from the sleeping area of the trailer.
products.bestFor: Fifth wheels with two air conditioners or a toy hauler load.
pros: 7,500 peak watts for two air conditioners
Dual fuel with a cast iron sleeve engine
cons: Only a peak figure is published
Heavy open frame needs a carrier or ramp

buyingCriteria.explanation: A fifth wheel often has two or three roof air conditioners, each drawing about 1,500 watts running and 2,500 to 3,000 at start. A 3,900 watt machine like the Westinghouse 5000 runs one. Two need about 6,000 running watts, which points to the AIVOLT 7500 or a larger unit. Soft start kits can let a smaller machine start two units, but they do not raise the running load, so two units still add up to about 3,000 watts running before any microwave or water heater joins in. Count every appliance that can run at once, not just the air conditioners.

A pickup's payload shrinks with a heavy pin weight on the hitch. The Genkins 4500 at 63 pounds is light, while an open-frame 7,500 watt machine can weigh well over 200 pounds. Add the weight of fuel, which is about 6 pounds per gallon, and check the number against the truck door sticker. Pin weight from the fifth wheel already eats a large share of payload, so every extra pound in the bed counts, and a generator carrier on a hitch can add tongue weight that the rig was not set up for. Weigh the loaded truck at a scale once, with the generator aboard, so you know the real margin rather than guessing from a sticker.

Many fifth wheels have a 50 amp inlet, but the generators here mostly offer a 30 amp outlet. The 30 amp circuit limits the draw to 3,600 watts at 120 volts. The AIVOLT 7500 offers a 120/240 volt outlet, which is closer to a 50 amp feed, but an adapter is still needed.

A fifth wheel's generator sits outside the coach, often in a truck bed. A key fob start, as on the Westinghouse 5000, saves a trip in the rain. Recoil units like the 4650 need a pull. Remote start needs a charged battery, so keep the charger handy and test the fob range at the actual site, since a coach with a metal skin can cut the signal in a way that surprises owners who only checked it in the driveway.

Propane stores for years and fits a fifth wheel that already carries two tanks. The AIVOLT 7500 is dual fuel, while the Westinghouse 5000 and Genkins 4500 are gasoline only. Propane output is lower than gasoline, so size for the weaker figure, and note that a fifth wheel with two 30 pound tanks has plenty of fuel for a generator that uses a separate small cylinder. Do not draw propane for the generator from the coach tanks without the proper regulator and fitting, because the coach system runs at a very different pressure from a generator hose.

Inverter machines give under 3 percent distortion and run quieter. The Westinghouse 5000 states under 3 percent. Open frames like the 4650 and the AIVOLT 7500 are louder and less suited to electronics. Pick by your campsite rules, because a generator that is not allowed to run after a certain hour is worth less than a smaller quiet one that is.

specDecoder.meaning: Rated is the continuous output; peak is a few seconds. A fifth wheel's air conditioners need the peak at start and the rated figure for the run.
specDecoder.watchFor: The AIVOLT 7500 lists only a peak figure, while the Genkins lists 4,500 peak and 3,800 rated.

specDecoder.meaning: A 30 amp, 120 volt RV receptacle for a standard shore cord. It carries up to 3,600 watts.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Westinghouse 5000 and 4650 both offer it.

specDecoder.meaning: A 120/240 volt, 30 amp outlet used for transfer switches and some RV adapters.
How clean the waveform is. Lower is better for electronics.
How long a tank lasts, usually at a light load.
specDecoder.watchFor: The 4650 claims up to 14 hours, the Genkins up to 8.

howWeEvaluated.title: Fit for a big trailer
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared rated watts against the demand of one to two roof air conditioners. The Westinghouse 5000 at 3,900 and Genkins at 3,800 suit one, while the AIVOLT 7500 is the only option for two.

howWeEvaluated.title: Truck bed practicality
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at weight and wheel kits. The Genkins at 63 pounds is the lightest, and the open-frame units need a ramp. Carrier ratings were considered.

howWeEvaluated.title: Starting and control
howWeEvaluated.description: Remote start on the Westinghouse 5000 was rated highest. Recoil on the 4650 and Genkins was rated lower, since a fifth wheel owner often starts the generator at the end of a long drive when patience is short.

howWeEvaluated.title: Fuel flexibility
howWeEvaluated.description: Propane support on the AIVOLT 7500 was weighed against gasoline-only designs. We recognized that propane lowers output, and we gave no credit for a dual fuel label where the listing gave no propane figure at all.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ownership and support
howWeEvaluated.description: Based on owner feedback patterns, we weighed brand support and parts. Westinghouse scored well, while newer brands such as Genkins and AIVOLT rely on warranty.

cards.label: Inverter (Westinghouse 5000, Genkins 4500)
cards.text: Quieter with clean power and lighter weight, and the engine slows down at night when only a fridge and lights are drawing power. The Westinghouse 5000 adds remote start, and the Genkins is the lightest at 63 pounds.

cards.label: Open frame (Westinghouse 4650, AIVOLT 7500)
cards.text: Cheaper per watt and longer on a tank, but louder and heavier, with a fixed engine speed that burns the same fuel at light load as at heavy load. The 4650 gives 14 hours claimed and the AIVOLT 7500 reaches 7,500 peak watts.

howToChoose.note: Choose inverter for campgrounds; choose open frame for remote sites and more output.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A big tank or propane supply, clean power for electronics, and an automatic CO shutoff. Plan fuel for a full week at your typical load.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Westinghouse 4650 with its four gallon tank is the long-runtime choice, and the AIVOLT 7500 gives propane flexibility.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You run two air conditioners or want remote start and clean power. The AIVOLT 7500 and Westinghouse 5000 each earn their cost in different ways.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You camp with hookups most nights and want a backup. The Westinghouse 4650 or Genkins 4500 keeps cost low.

maintenance.why: Small crankcases hold little oil. Low-oil shutdown stops the run.
Break-in debris collects early. Heavy summer loads shorten the interval.
Remote and electric starts need a healthy battery. A flat battery means a hard pull.
A loose generator shifts and can crack the tank or bend the frame. Use straps and a chock.
Gasoline gums carburetor jets. Run it dry or add stabilizer.

faq.q: How many watts do I need for a fifth wheel?
faq.a: One air conditioner and normal loads need about 3,500 watts. Two air conditioners need around 6,000 running watts plus the starting surge.

faq.q: Which is the best budget choice?
faq.a: The Westinghouse 4650 has the lowest cost per watt, and the Genkins 4500 offers a lighter inverter for a similar spend.

faq.q: Can a 30 amp outlet power a 50 amp fifth wheel?
faq.a: With an adapter, yes, but it limits the draw to 3,600 watts. That covers one air conditioner at a time.

faq.q: Is propane a good idea for a fifth wheel?
faq.a: Yes, since fifth wheels carry propane. The AIVOLT 7500 is the dual fuel option here. Expect lower output on propane.

faq.q: Can I carry a generator in the truck bed?
faq.a: Yes, but strap it down and keep it upright. Check the truck payload and never run a generator in the bed with a cover closed. Running it while it sits in the bed is also a fire and exhaust risk, so lift it down onto the ground, on level footing, before every start.

faq.q: Do I need a CO sensor?
faq.a: It is a worthwhile backup. The AIVOLT 7500 has a CO Watch-Guard. It does not replace keeping the generator away from windows and vents.
